post.caption:
At the peak of the 1637 mania a single tulip bulb traded for the price of an Amsterdam canal house, and buyers had stopped trading flowers and started trading contracts. Then one auction found no bidders and nothing about tulips had changed, only what people expected of tomorrow. The same shape recurs: South Sea, 1929, dot-com, 2008 housing. Recent historians think tulip mania was smaller and less damaging than the legend. The pattern is real, the story is exaggerated.
